label: M9 S3 | The DuPont Formula Arsenal — 3-Step and 5-Step

formulas.name: 3-Step DuPont Decomposition
formulas.formula: ROE = Net Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier

variables.meaning: Net Profit / Revenue — profitability per rupee of sales
Revenue / Total Assets — efficiency of asset utilisation
Total Assets / Shareholders' Equity — leverage multiplier; 1.0 = zero debt

formulas.worked_example: HUL FY23: Revenue = ₹58,154 Cr, Net Profit = ₹9,962 Cr, Total Assets = ₹24,200 Cr, Equity = ₹9,300 Cr. Net Margin = 9,962 / 58,154 = 17.1%. Asset Turnover = 58,154 / 24,200 = 2.40x. Equity Multiplier = 24,200 / 9,300 = 2.60x. Verification: ROE = 17.1% × 2.40 × 2.60 = 107% — matches HUL's reported ROE almost exactly. The decomposition tells the story: HUL earns elite ROE through extremely high margins (17.1% is outstanding for FMCG) combined with excellent asset turnover (2.4x reflects the asset-light model) and modest leverage (2.6x equity multiplier is driven by payables from distributors, not genuine debt — HUL is almost debt-free).
formulas.sensitivity_note: A 1 percentage point improvement in Net Margin on a base of 17% = 6% relative improvement. A 0.1x improvement in Asset Turnover on a base of 2.4x = 4% relative improvement. A 0.5x increase in Equity Multiplier = 19% relative improvement in ROE. Leverage has the highest sensitivity — and that's exactly why manipulating ROE with debt is so tempting and so dangerous.

formulas.name: 5-Step DuPont Decomposition
formulas.formula: ROE = Tax Burden × Interest Burden × Operating Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier

variables.meaning: Net Profit / Pre-Tax Profit — measures how much profit survives after tax (1 - tax rate)
Pre-Tax Profit / EBIT — measures how much operating profit survives after interest (1 = no interest cost; 0.7 = 30% consumed by interest)
EBIT / Revenue — pure operating profitability, stripped of financing and tax effects

formulas.worked_example: Tata Motors FY23 (standalone, approximate): EBIT = ₹4,200 Cr, Interest = ₹1,800 Cr, Pre-Tax Profit = ₹2,400 Cr, Tax = ₹600 Cr, Net Profit = ₹1,800 Cr. Revenue = ₹65,000 Cr, Total Assets = ₹85,000 Cr, Equity = ₹18,000 Cr. Tax Burden = 1,800/2,400 = 0.75. Interest Burden = 2,400/4,200 = 0.57 (this is low — a full 43% of operating profit is consumed by interest). Operating Margin = 4,200/65,000 = 6.5%. Asset Turnover = 65,000/85,000 = 0.76x. Equity Multiplier = 85,000/18,000 = 4.72x. ROE = 0.75 × 0.57 × 6.5% × 0.76 × 4.72 = 10.0%. The 5-step version exposes that Tata Motors' modest 10% ROE is being dragged down by a punishing interest burden — the company is earning operating profit but losing nearly half to interest payments. This is the kind of insight invisible in the 3-step version but obvious in the 5-step.
formulas.sensitivity_note: The 5-step is especially valuable for highly-leveraged companies where interest is a meaningful P&L item. If Interest Burden is below 0.7 (i.e. interest consumes more than 30% of EBIT), the company is financially stressed and this framework exposes exactly why ROE is weak despite decent operations.

formulas.name: 3-Step DuPont Decomposition
formulas.formula: ROE = Net Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier

variables.meaning: Return on Equity — net profit expressed as a percentage of shareholders' equity
Net Profit / Revenue — profitability per rupee of sales
Revenue / Total Assets — efficiency of asset utilisation
Total Assets / Shareholders' Equity — leverage multiplier; 1.0 = zero debt

formulas.plain_english: The 3-step DuPont breaks ROE into three independent drivers: how much profit the company squeezes from each rupee of sales, how efficiently it deploys assets to generate revenue, and how much it levers those assets with debt. This decomposition reveals whether a company's equity returns come from operational excellence (high margins, good turnover) or financial engineering (debt). For equity analysts in India, this is the fastest way to spot whether a firm's ROE is sustainable or debt-fuelled.
computation: Step 1: Calculate Net Margin = Net Profit ÷ Revenue
Step 2: Calculate Asset Turnover = Revenue ÷ Total Assets
Step 3: Calculate Equity Multiplier = Total Assets ÷ Shareholders' Equity
Step 4: Multiply all three ratios to verify ROE consistency

worked_example.problem: HUL FY23: Revenue = ₹58,154 Cr, Net Profit = ₹9,962 Cr, Total Assets = ₹24,200 Cr, Shareholders' Equity = ₹9,300 Cr. Decompose ROE into its three drivers.
worked_example.result: ROE = 107.0% matches HUL's reported ROE almost exactly.
worked_example.insight: HUL achieves elite ROE through three distinct competitive advantages: (1) Outstanding profitability — 17.1% net margin is exceptional in FMCG and reflects strong brand pricing power; (2) Excellent asset efficiency — 2.4x turnover reflects an asset-light model with significant outsourcing of manufacturing; (3) Conservative leverage — 2.6x equity multiplier is driven by operational payables to distributors, not genuine debt. HUL is nearly debt-free, meaning its ROE is sustainable and not at risk from interest burden or refinancing stress.

formulas.sensitivity_note: A 1 percentage point improvement in Net Margin on a base of 17% = 6% relative improvement. A 0.1x improvement in Asset Turnover on a base of 2.4x = 4% relative improvement. A 0.5x increase in Equity Multiplier = 19% relative improvement in ROE. Leverage has the highest sensitivity — and that's exactly why manipulating ROE with debt is so tempting and so dangerous.

formulas.name: 5-Step DuPont Decomposition
formulas.formula: ROE = Tax Burden × Interest Burden × Operating Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier

variables.meaning: Return on Equity — net profit as a percentage of shareholders' equity
Net Profit / Pre-Tax Profit — measures how much profit survives after tax (1 - effective tax rate)
Pre-Tax Profit / EBIT — measures how much operating profit survives after interest (1 = no interest cost; 0.7 = 30% consumed by interest)
EBIT / Revenue — pure operating profitability, stripped of financing and tax effects
Revenue / Total Assets — efficiency of asset utilisation
Total Assets / Shareholders' Equity — financial leverage

formulas.plain_english: The 5-step DuPont extends the 3-step by peeling back the 'Net Margin' layer into its constituent parts: how much of operating profit is lost to interest (Interest Burden) and how much of the remainder is lost to taxes (Tax Burden). This is invaluable when comparing highly-leveraged companies or those operating in different tax regimes. For Indian equity research, this decomposition immediately exposes whether weak ROE stems from weak operations, crippling interest costs, or unfavourable tax positions — each requiring a different investment thesis.
computation: Step 1: Calculate Tax Burden = Net Profit ÷ Pre-Tax Profit
Step 2: Calculate Interest Burden = Pre-Tax Profit ÷ EBIT
Step 3: Calculate Operating Margin = EBIT ÷ Revenue
Step 4: Calculate Asset Turnover = Revenue ÷ Total Assets
Step 5: Calculate Equity Multiplier = Total Assets ÷ Shareholders' Equity
Step 6: Multiply all five ratios to verify ROE consistency

worked_example.problem: Tata Motors FY23 (standalone): EBIT = ₹4,200 Cr, Interest Expense = ₹1,800 Cr, Pre-Tax Profit = ₹2,400 Cr, Tax = ₹600 Cr, Net Profit = ₹1,800 Cr, Revenue = ₹65,000 Cr, Total Assets = ₹85,000 Cr, Shareholders' Equity = ₹18,000 Cr. Decompose ROE into all five drivers.
steps: Tax Burden = ₹1,800 Cr ÷ ₹2,400 Cr = 0.750 (25% effective tax rate)
Interest Burden = ₹2,400 Cr ÷ ₹4,200 Cr = 0.571 (interest consumes 42.9% of EBIT)
worked_example.result: ROE = 10.0% — modest returns on equity despite 6.46% operating margin.
worked_example.insight: The 5-step decomposition exposes the true drag on Tata Motors' returns: while the company generates respectable 6.46% operating margins (acceptable for automotive manufacturing), a punishing interest burden of 0.571 consumes 42.9% of operating profit. This leaves only 57% of EBIT to cover taxes and flow to equity. Combined with moderate asset turnover (0.765x) and high leverage (4.72x multiplier), the result is a weak 10% ROE despite solid operational performance. For an equity analyst, this immediately signals that the investment case hinges on debt reduction — the operational machinery works fine, but financial stress is killing shareholder returns. This insight is completely invisible in the 3-step version but obvious in the 5-step.

formulas.sensitivity_note: The 5-step is especially valuable for highly-leveraged companies where interest is a meaningful P&L item. If Interest Burden falls below 0.70 (i.e. interest consumes more than 30% of EBIT), the company is in financial distress and this framework exposes exactly why ROE is weak despite decent operations. For Indian banks and NBFCs, watch Tax Burden closely due to variable tax regimes; for auto and steel companies, Interest Burden is often the dominant constraint on ROE.
